**Maintainability, transparency and verifiability: anonymized validation and bug reports, checkable security claims, CI and full project documentation.**

2.0.2 does not change what the toolkit does in your domain: the target state, the delegated rights and the setup steps are the same as in 2.0.1. It adds what others need to verify, report on and maintain the project.

> **Verification status.** The 2.x scripts pass parser, PSScriptAnalyzer, unit tests, an end-to-end test against a mocked AD module and the static security-claim checks in CI. The **end-to-end lab validation in a real domain (L1-L20) is in progress**. Validate in your own lab first. See [docs/VALIDATION.md](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.2/docs/VALIDATION.md).

## New

- **`Export-SoaReport.ps1`** collects the validation status (L1-L20) or bug-report data into a local, reviewable folder:
  - all required facts (OS builds and updates, agent version, topology, policy mode, script integrity);
  - identifiers replaced by stable pseudonyms; the map stays outside the folder;
  - a leak check, and packaging only after your review and confirmation (`-Package`);
  - manual results via `-Record`.

  Details: [docs/REPORTING.md](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.2/docs/REPORTING.md).
- **Security claims S1-S7** in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.2/SECURITY.md). Each one says where it is implemented and how to verify it, and there is a prompt for reviewing the repository with your own AI. `tools/Test-SoaSecurityClaims.ps1` checks the claims statically and lists every write operation.
- **Developer tooling and CI:**
  - `tools/Invoke-SoaStaticChecks.ps1`, repository hygiene (hidden / bidi characters, headers, version consistency);
  - `tools/Build-SoaRelease.ps1` (zip from the signed tag with `SHA256SUMS.txt`);
  - `tests/`;
  - GitHub Actions on PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1.
- **Project documentation:**
  - [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.2/AGENTS.md): rules for contributors and coding agents;
  - [docs/DECISIONS.md](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.2/docs/DECISIONS.md): design decisions;
  - [docs/EVIDENCE.md](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.2/docs/EVIDENCE.md): lab evidence;
  - [docs/MAINTENANCE.md](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.2/docs/MAINTENANCE.md), [docs/RELEASING.md](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.2/docs/RELEASING.md);
  - issue forms for bug reports and lab results.
- **README:** verification status with the open items, and a section *How this project was built*. The project was written with extensive AI assistance. The maintainer measured the *Observed* findings manually in a lab and reviews the artifacts.

## Fixed

- Windows PowerShell 5.1: reading `test-state.json` could produce a nested array, because `ConvertFrom-Json` does not enumerate arrays there. Earlier test results were lost or not shown. Fixed with `Read-SoaJsonArray`.

## Upgrade from 2.0.1

1. Replace the scripts with this release. Keep your `SoaToolkit.config.psd1`; there are no new keys.
2. Update the scripts on the hosts:
   ```powershell
   .\Install-SoaToolkit.ps1 -Step DeployTasks
   ```
3. Optional: check the claims yourself.
   ```powershell
   .\tools\Test-SoaSecurityClaims.ps1
   ```

Details: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.2/CHANGELOG.md)

## Verify the download

Compare the SHA-256 of the asset with the digest GitHub shows next to it. The zip contains `SHA256SUMS.txt` for every file:

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\cloudsync-soa-toolkit-2.0.2.zip -Algorithm SHA256
Get-ChildItem -Recurse | Unblock-File
```

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/compare/v2.0.1...v2.0.2
